# secopsctl soar

Operate Google SecOps SOAR (Siemplify) as code (AppKey auth, no ADC)

```text

```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|

## soar connector run

MUTATING (guarded): trigger a connector instance to pull on demand

> Guarded mutation — dry-run by default; apply with `--yes`.

```text
secopsctl soar connector run --integration X --connector Y --instance Z [flags]
```

```text
Run a connector instance once on demand — verify it pulls events after a
config change without waiting for its schedule. The three ids come from the
connector definition (`soar pull connectors`). Guarded: dry-run by default,
--yes to apply.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--connector` | string | - | connector definition id (required) |
| `--dry-run` | bool | false | preview only (default behavior) |
| `--instance` | string | - | connector instance id (required) |
| `--integration` | string | - | integration id (required) |
| `--yes` | bool | false | apply for real / skip confirmation |

## soar connector stat

Read-only: runtime statistics for one connector instance (events, errors, last run)

```text
secopsctl soar connector stat <identifier>
```

```text
Fetch runtime statistics for a connector instance by its identifier (from
`soar pull connectors`) — events processed, errors, and last-run timing, to
confirm a connector is healthy after a config change. JSON.
```

## soar ide build-playbook

Offline: compose a scheduled playbook from exported JSON molds

```text
secopsctl soar ide build-playbook --base <playbook.json> --cron <expr> --out <playbook.json> [flags]
```

```text
Build a save-ready SOAR playbook JSON file without calling SOAR.
Start from a full exported base playbook, set trigger.cronSchedule,
and optionally replace named placeholder steps with exported, already
wired integration-action step molds.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--base` | string | - | full exported base playbook JSON (required) |
| `--cron` | string | - | cron expression to set on trigger.cronSchedule (required) |
| `--name` | string | - | override playbook name |
| `--out` | string | - | output playbook JSON path (required) |
| `--replace-step` | stringArray | - | replace a base step with a mold: <step-name\|id>=<step.json> (repeatable) |

## soar legacy call

Call an external-API op, e.g. integrations/GetInstalledIntegrations

> Guarded mutation — dry-run by default; apply with `--yes`.

```text
secopsctl soar legacy call <op> [flags]
```

```text
op is the path under /api/external/v1 (leading slash optional). GET is
read-only. The legacy API uses POST for BOTH reads and writes, so a POST
must declare intent: --read for a read-only call, or --write for a mutation.
PUT/DELETE/--write print the LIVE banner and require --yes.

Discover ops with `secopsctl soar legacy list [--grep TEXT] [--tag TAG]`.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--body` | string | - | JSON file to send as the request body |
| `--dry-run` | bool | false | preview the composed request (method, op, body); send nothing |
| `--method` | string | GET | HTTP method (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) |
| `--out` | string | - | write the response to this file (0600) instead of stdout |
| `--read` | bool | false | assert a read-only POST (skips the mutation guard) |
| `--write` | bool | false | mark this call as mutating (LIVE banner + --yes); required for a write-POST |
| `--yes` | bool | false | confirm a mutating call |

## soar legacy list

List external-API ops for `legacy call` (offline, from the bundled index)

```text
secopsctl soar legacy list [--grep TEXT] [--tag TAG] [--method M] [flags]
```

```text
Browse the bundled, tenant-neutral index of Siemplify external-API
operations so `soar legacy call <op>` targets are discoverable without the
upstream swagger. Filters: --grep (substring over op/tag/summary),
--tag (exact, case-insensitive), --method (GET/POST/...). Reads nothing live.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--grep` | string | - | substring filter over op/tag/summary (case-insensitive) |
| `--method` | string | - | filter to one HTTP method (GET/POST/PUT/DELETE) |
| `--tag` | string | - | filter to one tag (case-insensitive), e.g. Cases, Jobs, Ontology |

## soar pull

Read-only: snapshot SOAR state to local files

```text
secopsctl soar pull <target> [flags]
```

```text
Targets: grouping, cases, blacklists, case-stages, case-tags, close-root-causes, connector-allowlist, connectors, environments, idp, jobs, networks, playbook-categories, playbooks, sla-definitions, soc-roles, tracking-lists, visual-families, webhooks, all.
Engine surfaces (blacklists, case-stages, case-tags, close-root-causes, connector-allowlist, connectors, environments, idp, jobs, networks, playbook-categories, playbooks, sla-definitions, soc-roles, tracking-lists, visual-families, webhooks) snapshot one
diff-friendly file per object for the pull->diff->push loop.

--prune removes local files whose live counterparts have been deleted,
so the mirror directory is an exact reflection of the instance. Refused
on an incomplete listing to prevent false deletions.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--out` | string | - | output root directory (default: cwd) |
| `--prune` | bool | false | remove local files with no live counterpart |

## soar push bulk-close

Bulk-close SOAR cases by id or by a filter (reason: malicious|not-malicious|maintenance|inconclusive|unknown)

> Guarded mutation — dry-run by default; apply with `--yes`.

```text
secopsctl soar push bulk-close [flags]
```

```text
Close many SOAR cases in one guarded command with a typed close-reason, root
cause, and comment. Select the cases by explicit ids (--ids) or by a modern
cases-list filter (--where), e.g. the stale/duplicate sets a case-hygiene job
would sweep. With --where, the matching cases are listed and counted before
the guard so the set is reviewable. Dry-run by default; --yes to apply.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--comment` | string | - | close comment |
| `--dry-run` | bool | false | preview only (default behavior) |
| `--ids` | string | - | comma-separated SOAR case ids (one of --ids/--where required) |
| `--reason` | string | maintenance | close reason: malicious \| not-malicious \| maintenance \| inconclusive \| unknown |
| `--root-cause` | string | - | close root cause |
| `--where` | string | - | modern cases-list filter selecting the cases to close (alternative to --ids) |
| `--yes` | bool | false | apply for real / skip confirmation |

**Examples**

```bash
# by id
  secopsctl soar push bulk-close --ids 101,102 --reason not-malicious

  # by filter: close a stale set with a root cause, reviewed first
  secopsctl soar push bulk-close \
      --where "status = 'OPENED' and priority = 'PRIORITY_LOW'" \
      --reason maintenance --root-cause 'Auto-closed: stale'
```

## soar push playbook

Save ONE playbook from a file (whole-body replace; mints a new version)

> Guarded mutation — dry-run by default; apply with `--yes`.

```text

the server mints a new version). This is NOT the directory reconcile — for that
use `soar push playbooks` (plural), which diffs the local playbooks/ folder
against live and supports --prune. Singular = save one file; plural = reconcile.
```

## soar settings api-keys

List, create (guarded), and revoke (guarded) SOAR API keys

```text
secopsctl soar settings api-keys
```

## soar settings api-keys create

MUTATING (guarded): create an API key — the secret is minted locally and printed ONCE

> Guarded mutation — dry-run by default; apply with `--yes`.

```text
secopsctl soar settings api-keys create --name <n> --permission-group N [flags]
```

```text
Register a new SOAR external-API key. The secret value is generated locally
(crypto/rand UUID — the server stores the supplied value and only ever shows
it masked afterwards), printed exactly once on success, and never persisted
or logged. Pick the least-privileged --permission-group for the key's job
(`soar pull soc-roles` and the web UI's Settings list the groups).
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | bool | false | preview only (default behavior) |
| `--environment` | stringSlice | [*] | environment scope (repeatable; default all) |
| `--name` | string | - | key name (required) |
| `--permission-group` | int | 0 | permission group id the key acts as (required) |
| `--soc-role` | int | 0 | SOC role id (0 = server default) |
| `--yes` | bool | false | apply for real / skip confirmation |

## soar settings api-keys list

List API keys: id, name, permission group, SOC role, environments, created

```text
secopsctl soar settings api-keys list
```

## soar settings api-keys revoke


|---|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | bool | false | preview only (default behavior) |
| `--id` | int | 0 | key id to revoke |
| `--name` | string | - | key name to revoke |
| `--yes` | bool | false | apply for real / skip confirmation |

## soar settings grouping get

Read the alert-grouping settings (max-alerts-per-case + any module properties)

```text
secopsctl soar settings grouping get
```

```text
Read the alert-grouping General/Overflow settings from the modern moduleSettings
property bag — Timeframe, max-alerts, overflow timeframe/max, grouping algorithm,
and source-grouping-identifier fallback (the same properties the SOAR Settings >
Alerts Grouping page shows) — plus the legacy max-alerts-per-case value.
```

## soar settings grouping set

MUTATING (guarded): set alert-grouping settings properties

> Guarded mutation — dry-run by default; apply with `--yes`.

```text
secopsctl soar settings grouping set --property <name>=<value> [--property ...] [flags]
```

```text
Set one or more alert-grouping settings properties by name=value, via the
modern moduleSettings bag — the same properties the SOAR Settings > Alerts
Grouping page edits. Property names come from `soar settings grouping get`
(e.g. TimeframeForGroupingInHours, MaxAGroupingForAlerts, OverflowMaxAGroupingForAlerts,
FallbackToSourceGroupingIdentifier). The dry-run preview shows each current ->
requested transition; unchanged properties are skipped. Guarded: dry-run by
default, --yes to apply (v1alpha on the SOAR host).
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | bool | false | preview only (default behavior) |
| `--property` | stringArray | - | a grouping setting as name=value (repeatable) |
| `--yes` | bool | false | apply for real / skip confirmation |

**Examples**

```bash
secopsctl soar settings grouping get
  secopsctl soar settings grouping set --property TimeframeForGroupingInHours=4 --dry-run
```

## soar users list

Read-only: list SOAR users (the USERNAME column is the value for `case assign --user`)

```text
secopsctl soar users list [--grep TEXT] [--all] [flags]
```

```text
List SOAR users so an assignee's id is discoverable for `soar case assign
--user <USERNAME>`. Disabled accounts are hidden unless --all. --grep filters
case-insensitively over username / name / email. Reads only; metadata only
(no avatar, no secret).
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--all` | bool | false | include disabled accounts (hidden by default) |
| `--grep` | string | - | filter over username/name/email (case-insensitive) |
